newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-PIPPEN, JORDAN LEAD WAY AS BULLS MAUL PISTONS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-PIPPEN, JORDAN LEAD WAY AS BULLS MAUL PISTONS.

text.p: The Detroit Pistons are one of the best teams in the National Basketball Association -- except when they play the Chicago Bulls.
Scottie Pippen had 26 points, despite sitting the entire fourth quarter, and Michael Jordan added 23 as the Bulls romped past Detroit 103-88 for their 19th consecutive win over the Pistons.
Luc Longley had 16 points and Steve Kerr chipped in 15 off the bench for Chicago, which extended its homecourt winning streak to 26 games.
"There is no question they are the best team in our league," conceded Detroit coach Doug Collins.
"They just thoroughly outplayed us tonight in every facet of the game," Collins said. "Barring any injury, the Bulls will win their fifth world title."
Grant Hill had 16 points and Otis Thorpe added 14 for Detroit.
Longley had six points in a 10-2 Chicago spurt to open the fourth quarter. Chicago's lead grew as large as 95-72 after Dennis Rodman nailed a three-pointer with 7:59 to go.
At Washington, Gheorghe Muresan's hook shot over Arvydas Sabonis with 19 seconds remaining lifted the Bullets to a 108-104 victory over the Trail Blazers, ending Portland's 11-game winning streak.
Chris Webber had 26 points, 12 rebounds and seven assists for Washington, winner of five of its last seven games.
Rod Strickland added 22 points and 11 assists and Muresan finished with 17 points for the Bullets. Isaiah Rider scored 28 points and Rasheed Wallace added 25 for Portland.
In Houston, Wesley Person's three-pointer with 1:53 to play snapped a tie and Rex Chapman scored 27 points to lead the Phoenix Suns to a 104-99 victory over the Rockets.
Kevin Johnson added 21 points for the Suns, who have won nine of their last 12 games and moved one-half game ahead of Sacramento for the final Western Conference playoff spot.

Jason Kidd recorded a triple double for Phoenix with 12 points, 10 rebounds and 15 assists. Hakeem Olajuwon led Houston with a game-high 39 points and Clyde Drexler had a triple double with 17 points, 10 rebounds and 11 assists.
In Charlotte, Dell Curry came off the bench to score 21 points and spark a pivotal 6-0 run midway through overtime as the Hornets beat the Golden State Warriors 100-93.
Glen Rice led Charlotte with 24 points and capped the overtime burst with a layup that put the Hornets ahead 97-91 with 68 seconds to go.
Muggsy Bogues added 17 and 12 assists for Charlotte.
Warriors forward Andrew DeClercq sent the game into overtime with a tip-in at the buzzer. Joe Smith led the Warriors with 31 points and 15 rebounds.
In Dallas, Tyrone Hill had 24 points and 18 rebounds and made a layup and free throw in the final 40 seconds to lead the Ceveland Cavaliers to a 75-72 victory over the Mavericks.
Danny Ferry scored 16 points and Bobby Phills added 13 for the Cavs, who occupy the eighth and final playoff spot in the Eastern Conference.
Michael Finley led Dallas with 22 points.
At Utah, Karl Malone scored 20 points and John Stockton added 19 as the Jazz cruised to a 107-94 victory over the Los Angeles Clippers.
Jeff Hornacek contributed 14 for Utah, winner of six in a row and 20 of its last 23 games.
Malik Sealy scored 19 points and Rodney Rogers added 18 for Los Angeles, which trailed by at least 13 points throughout the second half.
In Milwaukee, Armon Gilliam scored 20 points as the Bucks edged the New York Knicks 80-79 despite scoring just 10 points in the fourth quarter.
Vin Baker and Glenn Robinson added 16 points apiece for the Bucks. Patrick Ewing led the Knicks with 25 points.
New York had a chance to win in the closing seconds but Charlie Ward missed a floater in the lane and three or four tip-in attempts failed to drop for the Knicks.
In Seattle, Hersey Hawkins scored 22 points to lead seven players in double figures as the SuperSonics rolled over the Sacramento Kings 113-99.

Seattle All-Star guard Gary Payton was ejected 56 seconds into the second half for arguing a call after scoring just 13 points. But the Sonics' bench picked up the slack, outscoring Sacramento's subs, 53-31.
Mitch Richmond scored 25 points and Mahmoud Abdul-Rauf added 21 for Sacramento.
